meta.title: Compliance, AML, KYC & Ethics
meta.description: 195 MCQs covering Compliance Function, AML/CFT/CPF, KYC/UBO, Ethics, and Whistleblowing

modules.title: Module 1: Conduct & Compliance Group — Structure, Function, Culture
Module 3: Know Your Customer, CDD & Beneficial Owners

questionBank.q: What is the primary responsibility of the Compliance Function in a bank?
opts: Ensuring observance with all applicable laws, regulations, and corporate ethical standards.
Maximising return on equity through aggressive product innovation.
Directly managing the bank's daily treasury and liquidity operations.
Developing new customer-facing digital banking software features.
questionBank.exp: The Compliance Function ensures observance with policies, laws, regulations and corporate ethical standards (page 6).

questionBank.q: Which risk type is directly mitigated by a strong compliance function?
questionBank.exp: Compliance takes care of reputation and regulatory risks, and indirectly some aspects of operational risk (page 6).

questionBank.q: Which of the following correctly describes the two levels of business compliance?
opts: External rules imposed on the organisation and internal controls to achieve them.
Internal profit targets and external shareholder expectations.
Employee personal conduct and corporate social responsibility.
Regulatory capital requirements and liquidity coverage ratios.
questionBank.exp: Level 1 involves external rules; Level 2 involves internal systems to achieve compliance with external rules (page 6).

questionBank.q: What does 'Compliance risk' refer to in a banking context?
opts: The risk of impairment from failure to meet laws, regulations, and internal policies.
The risk of customer default on loan repayment obligations.
The risk of technology failure disrupting core banking systems.
The risk of currency devaluation affecting foreign investments.
questionBank.exp: Compliance risk is the risk of impairment to the business model, reputation and financial condition from failure to meet laws and internal standards (page 6).

questionBank.q: Which of the following is an internal source of compliance risk?
opts: Failure to adhere to the bank's Code of Conduct and Gifts Policy.
Enactment of a new Central Bank of Nigeria policy.
Amendment to the Companies and Allied Matters Act.
A new regulation from the Securities and Exchange Commission.
questionBank.exp: Internal sources include Code of Conduct, Gifts Policy, conflict of interest, and insider dealing (page 7).

questionBank.q: Which of the following is an external source of compliance risk?
questionBank.exp: External sources include laws, EFCC, NDLEA, CAMA, BOFIA, CBN Policies and SEC (page 7).

questionBank.q: A compliance officer is expected to possess which key personal attribute?
opts: Independence of judgement and a proactive attitude.
A high-risk appetite for proprietary trading.
A primary focus on short-term sales targets.
questionBank.exp: Required attributes include independence of judgement, neutrality, critical mind, and a proactive attitude (page 8).

questionBank.q: Why is confidentiality important for a compliance professional?
opts: To protect sensitive regulatory and enforcement interactions.
To share customer data with marketing teams.
To improve public relations through transparency.
questionBank.exp: Confidentiality and impartiality are key attributes, especially when dealing with regulators and law enforcement (page 8).

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a key objective of the compliance function?
opts: Safeguarding stakeholder interests and protecting the bank's reputation.
Maximising bonus payouts for the executive team.
questionBank.exp: Objectives include safeguarding stakeholders' interests, protecting reputation, and removing legal liability (page 9).

questionBank.q: What is the primary purpose of the Regulatory Surveillance Compliance Unit?
opts: Act as liaison on legislative matters and coordinate regulatory examinations.
Conduct enhanced due diligence on high-risk customers.
Monitor staff account transactions for irregularities.
Provide compliance training to branch staff.
questionBank.exp: The unit handles regulatory enquiries, acts as liaison, and coordinates regulatory examinations (page 10).

questionBank.q: The Financial Crimes Compliance Unit is primarily responsible for:
opts: Monitoring channels to prevent money laundering and terrorist financing.
Managing the bank's financial investment portfolio.
Approving all international trade finance transactions.
questionBank.exp: The unit ensures bank channels are not used for ML/TF/PF and monitors high-risk transactions and PEPs (page 10).

questionBank.q: Which unit is responsible for monitoring staff accounts and reviewing Suspicious Transaction Reports?
questionBank.exp: Financial Crimes Compliance Unit reviews STRs, sanctions screening, and staff account activity (page 10).

questionBank.q: The Head Office Compliance Unit is responsible for which activity?
opts: Certification of applications and monitoring of risk assets.
KYC review of new retail accounts.
Liaison between group office and subsidiaries.
questionBank.exp: It certifies applications, monitors risk assets, collateral, and unusual postings (page 10).

questionBank.q: Which unit handles Anti-Bribery and Corruption risk assessment and governance document management?
questionBank.exp: The Global Compliance Advisory Unit conducts ABC risk assessment and manages governance documents (page 11).

questionBank.q: The Retail Compliance Unit performs which of these duties?
opts: KYC review of new accounts and monitoring of branch control logs.
Monitoring the bank's correspondent banking relationships.
Managing the bank's anti-money laundering software.
questionBank.exp: The unit is responsible for KYC review, branch control logs, spot checks, and vault administration (page 11).

questionBank.q: The Subsidiaries Conduct & Compliance Unit acts as:
opts: The liaison between the Group Office and its subsidiaries.
The primary auditor for the bank's financial statements.
The head of retail sales across all branches.
The manager of the bank's electronic payment platforms.
questionBank.exp: It acts as the liaison between Group Office and subsidiaries, performing oversight of compliance monitoring (page 11).

questionBank.q: In the Three Lines of Defence model, which line owns and manages compliance risks?
questionBank.exp: The first line (businesses) owns and manages compliance risks and develops internal control frameworks (page 12).

questionBank.q: Which line of defence provides independent assurance that the risk management and control processes are effective?
questionBank.exp: The third line (Internal Audit) provides independent assurance on the effectiveness of risk management and controls (page 12).

questionBank.q: Who is legally mandated to be appointed as the Chief Compliance Officer under Nigerian law?
opts: A person not below the rank of General Manager at headquarters and at every branch.
A junior officer with compliance experience.
An external consultant on a short-term contract.
A member of the bank's internal audit team.
questionBank.exp: The Money Laundering Prohibition Act requires a CCO not below the rank of General Manager (page 14).

questionBank.q: To whom does the Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) report?
questionBank.exp: The Regulation mandates that the CCO reports to an Executive Compliance Officer (page 14).

questionBank.q: What is a primary responsibility of the Chief Compliance Officer?
opts: Advising senior management on laws, rules, and ethical standards.
Managing the bank's corporate social investment portfolio.
questionBank.exp: The CCO advises senior management on laws, ethical standards, and acts as an interface with regulators (page 14).

questionBank.q: The Chief Compliance Officer must be competent and knowledgeable regarding:
opts: Money laundering, terrorist financing risks, and the AML legal framework.
Real estate valuation and property management.
questionBank.exp: The CCO must be competent in ML/TF/PF issues, risks, and the legal framework (page 15).

questionBank.q: Which responsibility falls under the CCO's role in developing the AML Program?
opts: Developing policies to deter and detect money laundering and terrorist financing.
Setting the bank's prime lending rate.
questionBank.exp: The CCO develops policies designed to deter and detect ML/TF as part of the AML Program (page 16).

questionBank.q: What must be included in a clear corporate policy on AML?
opts: A prohibition against retaliation against employees who report violations.
A guarantee of no regulatory inspections.
A promise to ignore minor infractions.
A policy to share all customer data with competitors.
questionBank.exp: The AML policy must include a clear policy prohibiting retaliation against employees who report (page 16).

questionBank.q: When should AML procedures be updated by the CCO?
opts: When laws change, business operations change, or new risks are identified.
Whenever a new branch is opened.
Only when a fine is imposed by a regulator.
questionBank.exp: Procedures are updated when laws change, business changes, or new ML/TF risks are identified (page 17).

questionBank.q: What is required regarding AML training for employees?
opts: Training of appropriate employees with mandatory attendance records.
Voluntary online training without attendance tracking.
Training only for new staff, not existing ones.
questionBank.exp: The CCO must ensure training of appropriate employees, with mandatory attendance and record-keeping (page 17).

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a component of an effective compliance program?
opts: A designated Chief Compliance Officer and internal policies and procedures.
A single employee handling all compliance duties without oversight.
Exclusive reliance on external lawyers for all decisions.
No need for employee training since rules are obvious.
questionBank.exp: Components include a designated CCO, internal policies, KYC, training, document retention, and independent testing (page 18).

questionBank.q: What defines a strong 'compliance culture' within an organisation?
opts: Established by top management and characterised by their example.
Delegated entirely to the human resources department.
Defined solely by the number of disciplinary actions taken.
Focused on profit maximisation over regulatory adherence.
questionBank.exp: A good compliance culture is established by top management, led by senior management example, and embedded in processes (page 19).

questionBank.q: What is the 'Confirmation' step in compliance risk management?
opts: Monitoring and testing the adequacy of controls and processes.
Creating awareness of policies and regulations.
Closing gaps identified by product owners.
questionBank.exp: Confirmation includes monitoring and testing adequacy of controls and processes (page 20).

questionBank.q: Which department is a key partner for Compliance in handling special investigations and audit reviews?
questionBank.exp: Compliance co-operates with Internal Audit for audit reviews, special investigations, and risk assessments (page 22).

questionBank.q: How does Human Resources assist the Compliance function?
opts: Implementing internal regulations and training sensitive staff.
Performing regulatory reporting to the CBN.
questionBank.exp: HR implements internal regulations, code of conduct, and provides information/training for staff (page 22).

questionBank.q: Which unit is responsible for ensuring statutory returns are sent to regulatory bodies on time?
questionBank.exp: The CCO must ensure all statutory returns are sent to required regulatory bodies as at when due (page 14).

questionBank.q: What is a key characteristic of the compliance mandate regarding the bank's business model?
opts: To embed compliance in the system to optimise efficiency.
To avoid any interaction with regulators.
questionBank.exp: The mandate includes optimising efficiency by embedding compliance in the system (page 13).

questionBank.q: Why might a bank suffer reputation damage even without a formal regulatory sanction?
opts: Significant adverse publicity from non-compliance can damage reputation independently.
Sanctions are the only cause of reputation damage.
Reputation is not affected by compliance matters.
Only the CBN can cause reputation damage.
questionBank.exp: Failure to adhere may result in significant adverse publicity and reputation damage even without a sanction (page 14).

questionBank.q: What is the role of the CCO regarding policy deficiencies?
opts: Identify deficiencies and formulate proposals for amendments.
Ignore deficiencies unless reported by customers.
Wait for regulators to point them out.
Delegate all policy reviews to junior staff.
questionBank.exp: The CCO identifies deficiencies in policies and formulates proposals for amendments (page 14).

questionBank.q: Money laundering is defined as the conversion or transfer of property knowing it is derived from:
opts: A criminal offence for the purpose of concealing its illicit origin.
A legitimate business venture for tax optimisation.
A family inheritance subject to estate duties.
questionBank.exp: Money laundering involves converting property knowing it is derived from a criminal offence to conceal its origin (page 24).

questionBank.q: Which act is NOT typically considered a money laundering predicate offence?
opts: Payment of utility bills from salary income.
questionBank.exp: Predicate offences include drug trafficking, corruption, counterfeiting, fraud, and terrorism — not legitimate salary spending (page 28).

questionBank.q: Money laundering is regarded as a 'catch-all' offence because:
opts: It encompasses aiding, abetting, concealing, and participating in criminal proceeds.
It only applies to bank managers.
questionBank.exp: It includes concealment, possession, transfer, receipt, participation, conspiracy, aiding and abetting (page 24).

questionBank.q: Deception is the art of money laundering. What is money laundering itself?
opts: A derivative crime that cannot exist without a prior criminal act.
A regulatory requirement for bank audits.
A type of tax evasion only.
A legal method of wealth management.
questionBank.exp: Money laundering is a derivative crime — it depends on a prior criminal offence (page 24).

questionBank.q: What does 'wilful blindness' mean in the context of money laundering?
opts: Deliberate avoidance of obvious facts indicating money laundering.
Failing to report a small cash deposit.
questionBank.exp: Wilful blindness is the deliberate avoidance of obvious facts (page 24).

questionBank.q: Which is the correct order of the three stages of money laundering?
questionBank.exp: The stages are Placement (entry), Layering (concealment), and Integration (appears legitimate) (page 26).

questionBank.q: During which stage of money laundering are illegal proceeds first introduced into the financial system?
questionBank.exp: Placement is the stage where illegal proceeds are placed into the financial system (page 26).

questionBank.q: Which money laundering stage involves complex transactions to conceal the origin of funds?
questionBank.exp: Layering involves multiple layers of transactions and wire transfers to conceal the origin and complicate tracing (page 26).

questionBank.q: At the Integration stage of money laundering, funds are:
questionBank.exp: Integration is when illegal funds are cleansed and now appear legitimate (page 26).

questionBank.q: What is the primary motivation difference between money laundering and terrorist financing?
opts: Money laundering is profit-driven; terrorist financing is ideologically driven.
Money laundering is smaller in scale.
Terrorist financing uses only legitimate funds.
There is no difference in motivation.
questionBank.exp: ML is motivated by profit, while TF is motivated by ideology (page 34).

questionBank.q: What is a key difference in the source of funds between money laundering and terrorist financing?
opts: ML uses illegitimate funds; TF can use both legitimate and illegitimate funds.
ML uses only cash; TF uses only digital assets.
TF uses only illegal drug money.
questionBank.exp: ML sources are illegitimate; TF sources can be legitimate and illegitimate (page 34).

questionBank.q: How does the money trail differ between money laundering and terrorist financing?
opts: ML is circular (returns to origin); TF is linear (used to propagate activities).
ML is linear; TF is circular.
questionBank.exp: ML money trail is circular (ends with originator); TF is linear (used for group/activities) (page 34).

questionBank.q: Which conduit is favoured by money launderers according to the comparison table?
questionBank.exp: Money laundering favours formal financial systems, while TF favours cash couriers and informal systems (page 34).

questionBank.q: What is a typical 'red flag' for money laundering?
opts: Transactions that appear uncharacteristic compared to prior account activity.
questionBank.exp: Red flags are suspicious activities uncharacteristic when compared with prior knowledge and expectations (page 34).

questionBank.q: Proliferation financing is motivated by:
questionBank.exp: Proliferation financing is ideologically driven (page 34).

questionBank.q: Under Section 34 of the AML/CFT/CPF Regulation 2022, when must a financial institution forward a suspicious transaction report to the NFIU?
questionBank.exp: The report must be forwarded to NFIU within 72 hours (page 35).

questionBank.q: What is the mandatory content required when filing a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR)?
opts: Account opening package, statements, customer info, source documents, and investigation report.
Only the customer's name and address.
questionBank.exp: Mandatory uploads include account opening package, statements, InfoPool pages, source documents, and investigation report (page 35).

questionBank.q: Which system is used to log Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) internally?
questionBank.exp: Staff log on to Processmaker, click New Case, and select Monitor Suspicious Transaction (Log STR) (page 35).

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a red flag for terrorist financing?
opts: Fund transfers ordered in small amounts to avoid triggering reporting.
Large single-deposit transactions from known businesses.
questionBank.exp: Small transfers to avoid reporting thresholds are a TF red flag (page 30).

questionBank.q: What is a red flag related to terrorist financing and charitable organisations?
opts: Financial transactions with no logical economic purpose or link to stated activity.
questionBank.exp: Red flags include transactions with no logical economic purpose or link to the NGO/charity's stated activity (page 30).

questionBank.q: Which is a red flag for terrorist financing concerning account dormancy?
opts: Periods of dormancy possibly resulting from terrorist training or combat engagement.
questionBank.exp: Dormancy could be the result of terrorist training or engagement in combat (page 30).

questionBank.q: A 'many-to-one' transaction cluster where many low-value transactions are received into one account is a red flag for:
questionBank.exp: Many-to-one transaction clusters can indicate fundraising activity (page 31).

questionBank.q: If a customer is on the United Nations 1267 Sanctions list, this is a red flag for:
questionBank.exp: Inclusion on the UN 1267 Sanctions list is a specific TF/PF red flag (page 31).

questionBank.q: What is the maximum single deposit amount and cumulative balance for a Tier 1 account under the tiered KYC?
opts: N50,000 deposit and N300,000 cumulative balance.
N100,000 deposit and N500,000 cumulative balance.
questionBank.exp: Tier 1 allows N50k deposit max and N300k cumulative balance (page 38).

questionBank.q: What is the maximum single deposit amount for a Tier 2 account under the tiered KYC?
questionBank.exp: Tier 2 has a maximum single deposit of N100,000 (page 38).

questionBank.q: Tier 3 accounts have which of the following features?
opts: No limit to cumulative balance, deposits, or transactions.
questionBank.exp: Tier 3 accounts have no limit to cumulative balance, deposit, or transactions (page 38).

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a basic requirement for opening a Tier 1 account?
opts: Basic customer information without mandatory verification evidence.
Full KYC documentation with independent verification.
questionBank.exp: Tier 1 requires basic customer information (passport, name, etc.) without verification evidence (page 38).

questionBank.q: International transfers are strictly prohibited for which tiers?
questionBank.exp: International transfers are prohibited for Tier 1, 2, and 3 (page 38).

questionBank.q: Terrorist financing is defined by FATF as:
opts: The financing of terrorist acts, terrorists, and terrorist organisations.
The support of peaceful religious activities.
questionBank.exp: FATF defines TF as the financing of terrorist acts, terrorists, and terrorist organisations (page 29).

questionBank.q: What is a common red flag involving Foreign Exchange (FX) transactions?
opts: FX transactions followed by immediate fund transfers to higher-risk locations.
FX transactions for import of essential goods.
FX transactions for student tuition payments.
questionBank.exp: Transactions involving FX followed by immediate transfers to higher-risk locations is a red flag (page 30).

questionBank.q: What should a bank do when it notices any of the AML red flags?
opts: Ignore it if the amount is small.
questionBank.exp: Your responsibility is to file STR when any red flag is noticed (page 31).

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a prohibited activity for the Bank regarding customers?
opts: Dealing with customers that trade in weapons of mass destruction (WMDs).
Dealing with customers that import agricultural equipment.
Dealing with students paying tuition fees.
questionBank.exp: The Bank prohibits business with customers trading in WMDs, illicit drugs, arms, human trafficking, etc. (page 51).

questionBank.q: Crypto transactions are now permitted subject to:
opts: Meeting the CBN requirements on Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs).
A minimum balance of N1 billion.
Approval from the Securities and Exchange Commission only.
A special license from the Nigerian Communications Commission.
questionBank.exp: Crypto is permitted subject to CBN requirements for VASPs (page 51).

questionBank.q: Which countries are listed as special risk areas for the Bank's business?
opts: Crimea, Donetsk, Luhansk, DPRK, Syria, Cuba, Iran, Yemen, Russia, Belarus.
questionBank.exp: The special risk areas include Crimea, Donetsk, Luhansk, DPRK, Syria, Cuba, Iran, Yemen, Russia, and Belarus (page 51).

questionBank.q: What type of customer does the Bank prohibit doing business with?
questionBank.exp: The Bank does not do business with shell companies (page 51).

questionBank.q: Hawala is a channel that the Bank prohibits because it is associated with:
opts: High risk of money laundering and terrorist financing.
Lack of regulatory clarity in Nigeria.
questionBank.exp: Hawala is listed as a prohibited channel due to ML/TF risks (page 51).

questionBank.q: Who must a financial institution verify the identity of before opening an account?
questionBank.exp: The FI must verify customer identity and beneficial ownership/control (page 47).

questionBank.q: What is the new mandatory requirement for individual account holders under the latest regulations?
opts: Tax Identification Number (TIN), date of birth, and telephone number.
questionBank.exp: TIN, date of birth, and telephone number are now mandatory for individuals (page 48).

questionBank.q: How can a financial institution verify telephone numbers for KYC?
opts: By independent process including validation against the NCC database or geo-mapping.
questionBank.exp: Verification can be via NCC database or geo-mapping (page 48).

questionBank.q: What must a financial institution do if performing Customer Due Diligence (CDD) might tip off the customer?
opts: Not pursue the CDD process and file an STR to NFIU immediately.
Call the customer to warn them.
questionBank.exp: The FI shall not pursue CDD and shall file an STR immediately (page 49).

questionBank.q: How often should CDD information be updated for high-risk customers?
questionBank.exp: For high-risk customers, every 12 months; moderate 18 months; low 3 years (page 49).

questionBank.q: What should a financial institution do with a Foreign Trust or Foundation that is opaque?
opts: Decline to open an account for the legal arrangement.
Open the account with basic information.
questionBank.exp: If opaque and information cannot be provided (e.g., tax havens), the FI shall decline to open an account (page 49).

questionBank.q: Refugees and asylum seekers can be banked using identification issued by:
opts: The Nigerian Immigration Service or other recognised government agency.
Only the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees.
questionBank.exp: Refugees can use identification issued by the Nigerian Immigration Service or other recognised government agency (page 50).

questionBank.q: What is the record retention period for transactions under the CBN AML Regulations?
opts: At least five years after completion of the transaction.
questionBank.exp: The bank must keep records for at least five years after the transaction is completed (page 80).

questionBank.q: What is the penalty for failure to maintain necessary transaction records?
questionBank.exp: The Bank shall be liable to a fine of N10 Million for failure to maintain records (page 80).

questionBank.q: What is the primary purpose of Know Your Customer (KYC) due diligence?
opts: To identify customers and ascertain relevant information for doing financial business with them.
To determine the profitability of each customer.
To assess the customer's credit score.
To market new products to the customer.
questionBank.exp: KYC is the due diligence to identify customers and ascertain relevant information for doing financial business (page 40).

questionBank.q: According to KYC principles, who does 'Customer' refer to?
opts: A real person or organisation that the Bank deals with, whether or not they have an account.
questionBank.exp: A customer includes anyone the Bank deals with, whether they have an account or not (page 40).

questionBank.q: What does 'Know' refer to in KYC principles?
opts: The identity, beneficial ownership, sources of funds, and nature of the customer's business.
questionBank.exp: Know means identity, BO, source of funds, nature of business, and reasonable account activity (page 40).

questionBank.q: Who is responsible for 'Knowing' the customer under the KYC framework?
opts: Account Officers and Relationship Managers (the Business).
questionBank.exp: Account Officers and Relationship Managers are responsible (page 40).

questionBank.q: What is a beneficial owner under Nigerian AML regulations?
opts: A natural person who ultimately owns or controls at least 5% of shares or voting rights.
The first listed director on the board.
questionBank.exp: A BO is a natural person who owns at least 5% of shares, exercises 5% voting rights, or controls the entity (page 53).

questionBank.q: Which document is NOT typically a source for determining beneficial ownership?
questionBank.exp: Sources include certificate of incorporation, MEMART, minutes, partnership agreements, and annual returns — not daily bank statements (page 53).

questionBank.q: What is a 'Legal Person' for the purpose of beneficial ownership identification?
opts: Corporate bodies, foundations, partnerships, associations, cooperatives, or similar entities.
A natural person with a bank account.
A minor child of a customer.
questionBank.exp: Legal persons include corporate bodies, foundations, partnerships, associations, cooperatives, or similar entities (page 54).

questionBank.q: What is a 'Legal Arrangement' in the context of CDD?
opts: Trusts, express trusts, or similar relationships separating legal ownership from beneficial ownership.
A joint venture with a foreign entity.
questionBank.exp: Legal arrangements include trusts separating legal ownership from beneficial ownership (page 54).

questionBank.q: Why is it crucial to identify legal persons in banking relationships?
opts: To mitigate ML/TF risks, as opaque legal persons are used to hide beneficial ownership.
To increase the bank's tax liability.
questionBank.exp: Effective identification of legal persons is crucial to mitigating ML/TF risk (page 54).

questionBank.q: What is a 'beneficiary' in the context of a trust?
opts: The individual or entity entitled to receive benefits or income from the trust assets.
The person who sets up the trust.
The person who manages the trust.
questionBank.exp: Beneficiaries are entitled to receive the benefits or income generated by trust assets (page 55).

questionBank.q: What is an 'intermediary' in a financial context?
opts: A middleman such as a bank or broker facilitating the flow of funds between savers and borrowers.
questionBank.exp: Intermediaries include banks and brokers that facilitate funds between savers and borrowers (page 55).

questionBank.q: Which type of trust is commonly used for estate planning and wealth management?
opts: Legal trusts governed by a trust deed.
questionBank.exp: Trusts are governed by a trust deed and commonly used for estate planning and wealth management (page 56).

questionBank.q: What is a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) commonly used for?
opts: To isolate specific assets or liabilities, often for securitisation and risk management.
To manage the bank's employee payroll.
questionBank.exp: SPVs isolate specific assets/liabilities and are used for financing and risk management (page 56).

questionBank.q: What due diligence is required for an SPV?
opts: Identify and verify the originator, sponsors, investors, collateral manager, and purpose of the SPV.
Only the name of the SPV.
questionBank.exp: Due diligence requires identifying the originator, sponsors, investors, collateral manager, and purpose (page 56).

questionBank.q: What is a red flag for identifying beneficial owners?
opts: A shareholders' agreement showing one natural person controls shares of more than one shareholder.
questionBank.exp: Red flags include nominee agreements, shareholders' agreements showing control, and dominant influence over transactions (page 57).

questionBank.q: What is the Bank's obligation regarding the UBO register?
opts: Create, maintain, and continually update it with information collected through CDD.
Create it once and never update it.
Share it publicly on the website.
questionBank.exp: The bank must create, maintain, and continually update the UBO register (page 57).

questionBank.q: What is a 'Politically Exposed Person' (PEP) as defined by FATF?
opts: An individual entrusted with a prominent public function.
Any member of a royal family.
questionBank.exp: A PEP is an individual entrusted with a prominent public function (page 61).

questionBank.q: Why are PEPs considered high risk for financial institutions?
opts: Their position and influence can be abused for money laundering and corruption.
They are not subject to any laws.
questionBank.exp: Their positions can be abused for ML and predicate offences like corruption (page 61).

questionBank.q: Which of the following is considered a 'Close Associate' (RCA) of a PEP?
opts: Business partners who share beneficial ownership of legal entities with the PEP.
A neighbour who occasionally waves hello.
questionBank.exp: RCAs include business partners and associates sharing beneficial ownership of legal entities (page 62).

questionBank.q: Who qualifies as a 'Relative and Close Associate' of a PEP?
opts: Spouses, partners, parents, children, siblings, and close friends.
All employees of the PEP's company.
All shareholders of the PEP's company.
All residents of the PEP's neighbourhood.
questionBank.exp: RCAs include spouses, parents, children, siblings, close friends, and legal advisors (page 62).

questionBank.q: Which Nigerian official would be classified as a PEP?
opts: A Senator in the National Assembly.
A junior clerk in the ministry.
questionBank.exp: Elected politicians such as Senators, House of Reps, and Councillors are PEPs (page 63).

questionBank.q: What rank of military officer is classified as a PEP?
opts: Colonel and above, and equivalents in Navy, Air Force, Police, Customs, Immigration.
Only the Chief of Defence Staff.
questionBank.exp: Senior Officers from the rank of Colonel and above are PEPs (page 63).

questionBank.q: Which approval level is required for onboarding a PEP relationship?
opts: Senior Management approval not below General Manager (GM).
Approval by the Customer Service Officer.
questionBank.exp: PEP onboarding requires Senior Management approval not below GM (page 66).

questionBank.q: What is the transaction threshold requiring GM approval for a PEP account?
questionBank.exp: Transactions of N5m/$30k require approval from GM and above (page 66).

questionBank.q: What Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) measure must be taken for a PEP?
opts: Establish the source of wealth and source of funds, and conduct enhanced ongoing monitoring.
Only collect a copy of the passport.
No extra steps beyond standard CDD.
Send the customer a questionnaire once a year.
questionBank.exp: EDD for PEPs includes establishing source of wealth/funds and enhanced monitoring (page 65).

questionBank.q: What should be done when a customer is identified as a PEP after onboarding?
opts: Conduct EDD, obtain senior management approval, and flag the account in the core banking system.
Ignore it since they were already onboarded.
Report to the police without internal approval.
questionBank.exp: EDD, senior management approval, and flagging in the core application are required (page 66).

questionBank.q: What is a common reason PEPs are not detected and flagged?
opts: Negligence or inadequate KYC by the Account Officer.
The bank's system is too sensitive.
The law does not require detection.
questionBank.exp: Reasons include negligence, improper profiling, concealment by AO, and knowledge gaps (page 64).

questionBank.q: What is a consequence of not identifying a PEP relationship?
opts: Imposition of fines, reputation risk, and potential severance by correspondent banks.
The customer automatically becomes low risk.
questionBank.exp: Consequences include fines, reputational damage, and loss of correspondent banking relationships (page 64).

questionBank.q: What is a Non-Governmental Organisation (NGO) in the context of banking risk?
opts: A non-profit entity with high public trust that can be abused for TF/ML.
questionBank.exp: NGOs are non-profit, have public trust, and can be used as proxies for TF/ML (page 67).

questionBank.q: Why are NGOs considered high risk by financial institutions?
opts: Their purpose can be abused toward funding terrorism and money laundering.
They have no board of directors.
questionBank.exp: The purpose of NGOs can be abused towards funding terrorism, ML, and PF (page 67).

questionBank.q: What is required when onboarding an NGO as a customer?
opts: Obtain the UBO and ED approval, mark as HIGH RISK and NGO in FCUBS, and continuously monitor.
questionBank.exp: UBO and ED approval, HIGH RISK tagging, and continuous monitoring are required (page 67).

questionBank.q: What is the purpose of FATCA (Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act) screening?
opts: To identify US citizens or residents for reporting to US tax authorities.
To screen for money laundering only.
questionBank.exp: FATCA screens for US nationality/residency for reporting to US tax authorities (page 68).

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a FATCA indication that triggers further due diligence?
opts: A US place of birth or US telephone number.
questionBank.exp: Indications include US nationality, US address, US place of birth, and US telephone number (page 68).

questionBank.q: What is the consequence for a Foreign Financial Institution that refuses to comply with FATCA?
opts: Application of 30% withholding tax on US source payments.
questionBank.exp: Refusal may result in 30% withholding tax (page 68).

questionBank.q: What is the role of the Branch Manager (BM) in FATCA compliance?
opts: Sight the customer, verify ID, ensure forms are filled, confirm MIS classification, and authorise maintenance.
Only sign off on loan applications.
questionBank.exp: The BM sights the customer, verifies ID, ensures forms, confirms MIS classification, and authorises (page 69).

questionBank.q: What is the CCO's role regarding FATCA?
opts: Ensure forms are filled, obtain ID validating US citizenship, and update the customer's MIS classification.
questionBank.exp: CCO ensures forms, obtains US ID, and updates MIS classification for FATCA (page 69).

questionBank.q: What is the mandate of the Special Control Unit Against Money Laundering (SCUML)?
opts: To monitor, supervise, and regulate all Designated Non-Financial Institutions (DNFIs).
To prosecute all money laundering cases.
questionBank.exp: SCUML monitors, supervises, and regulates DNFIs (page 70).

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a Designated Non-Financial Institution (DNFI) that must register with SCUML?
opts: Automobile dealers and dealers in precious metals.
questionBank.exp: DNFIs include automobile dealers, dealers in precious stones/metals, casinos, real estate dealers, etc. (page 72).

questionBank.q: What is prohibited when registering a customer on the SCUML platform?
opts: Collecting any form of gratification to register the customer's business.
Guiding the customer on the registration portal.
Using the customer's own email address.
Referring the customer to the SCUML helpdesk.
questionBank.exp: Never collect any gratification to register the customer's business (page 70).

questionBank.q: Which of the following is NOT a type of NGO orientation mentioned?
questionBank.exp: Types include Charitable, Service, Participatory, and Empowering — not profit maximisation (page 67).

questionBank.q: How does the Bank classify all PEP accounts?
questionBank.exp: In Access Bank, all PEP accounts are classified as high risk (page 61).

questionBank.q: What is a 'Blind Trust' and what must a financial institution do with it?
opts: Obtain and understand the Trust Agreement to identify grantor, settlor, trustor, and beneficiary.
questionBank.exp: FIs shall obtain and understand the Trust Agreement in a Blind Trust (page 49).

questionBank.q: How should a financial institution handle correspondent banking when the correspondent bank fails to provide satisfactory answers?
opts: Terminate the account with the correspondent bank.
Continue the relationship with reduced oversight.
questionBank.exp: If a correspondent fails to provide satisfactory answers, the FI shall terminate the account (page 50).

questionBank.q: What is required for non-face-to-face customers (internet banking) under CDD regulations?
opts: Conduct regular monitoring and use computerized monitoring systems to recognize unusual transactions.
questionBank.exp: Regular monitoring and computerized systems must be used for internet-based customers (page 50).

questionBank.q: Which statement best describes the CDD process for trusts?
opts: Identify and verify the settlor, trustee, protector, beneficiaries, and those exercising effective control.
questionBank.exp: Due diligence requires identifying settlor, trustee, protector, beneficiaries, and controllers (page 56).

questionBank.q: What is the purpose of maintaining a Beneficial Ownership register?
opts: To record information collected through CDD and flag inconsistencies to the CAC.
questionBank.exp: The register records BO information and flags inconsistencies to the CAC (page 57).

questionBank.q: What should be done if there is a discrepancy between the UBO register and records?
opts: Flag and report to the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC).
questionBank.exp: Flag and report inconsistency to the CAC (page 57).

questionBank.q: What is the EDD requirement for a customer with a multi-layered UBO structure?
opts: Conduct EDD on the entire chain of ownership until the true individuals are identified.
questionBank.exp: EDD shall be conducted to the entire chain of ownership until the true UBOs are identified (page 60).

questionBank.q: What is the minimum ownership threshold (5%) used for identifying beneficial owners?
questionBank.exp: The threshold is 5% of issued shares or voting rights (page 53).

questionBank.q: What is a 'Legal Trust' primarily used for?
opts: Estate planning, wealth management, and asset protection.
questionBank.exp: Trusts are used for estate planning, wealth management, and asset protection (page 56).

questionBank.q: What does the regulation require for verifying customer identity through telephone numbers?
opts: Validation against the NCC database or geo-mapping.
A sworn affidavit from the customer.
A letter from the customer's employer.
questionBank.exp: Telephone numbers must be validated against NCC database or geo-mapping (page 48).

questionBank.q: What is the procedure for opening an external or non-resident non-Nigerian account?
opts: Satisfy that the customer is permanently resident outside Nigeria per CBN Foreign Exchange Manual.
questionBank.exp: Per Memorandum 17 of the CBN Foreign Exchange Manual, satisfy they are permanently resident outside Nigeria (page 48).

questionBank.q: What is the key CDD requirement for refugees and asylum seekers?
opts: Use identification from Nigerian Immigration Service or recognised government agency.
Require a UNHCR refugee card only.
Require a letter from the embassy.
questionBank.exp: Use identification issued by the Nigerian Immigration Service or other recognisable government agency (page 50).

questionBank.q: What is the bank's policy regarding customers who trade in narcotics or illicit drugs?
opts: The Bank prohibits doing business with such customers.
The Bank allows it with enhanced monitoring.
The Bank only reports to NFIU but allows it.
The Bank encourages it for profit.
questionBank.exp: The Bank prohibits and does not do business with customers trading in narcotics/illicit drugs (page 51).

questionBank.q: What is required for FATCA screening of new customers?
opts: Screen each new customer against the seven FATCA indications at onboarding.
Only screen if the customer mentions US ties.
questionBank.exp: Screen each new customer against the seven FATCA indications at onboarding (page 68).

questionBank.q: What is the responsibility of the Bank regarding BOs that pose higher risk?
opts: Conduct EDD and file STR with NFIU if there are reasonable grounds to suspect ML/TF.
questionBank.exp: Conduct EDD and file STR if reasonable grounds to suspect ML/TF exist (page 57).

questionBank.q: How often are AML/CFT/CPF internal policies and procedures required to be updated?
opts: Annually to mitigate identified risks relating to BO.
Only when a new law is passed.
questionBank.exp: Annual update of AML/CFT/CPF internal policies to mitigate risks relating to BO is required (page 57).

questionBank.q: What is a 'Code of Ethics' in an organisational context?
opts: A written document stating acceptable and unacceptable behaviours for employees.
questionBank.exp: A Code of Ethics is a written document stating what acceptable and unacceptable behaviours are (page 74).

questionBank.q: What does 'Business Ethics' examine?
opts: Ethical principles or problems that arise in a business environment.
The technical specifications of banking software.
The architectural design of bank buildings.
questionBank.exp: Business ethics examines ethical principles or problems that arise in a business environment (page 74).

questionBank.q: What is the foundation upon which the Bank's ethical standards stand?
opts: Obeying the laws, rules, and regulations in letter and in spirit.
questionBank.exp: Obeying laws, rules, and regulations, both in letter and spirit, is the foundation (page 75).

questionBank.q: How long does the duty of confidentiality continue after an officer disengages from the Bank?
opts: Without limit in point of time.
Until the officer is hired elsewhere.
questionBank.exp: Confidentiality restriction continues without limit in time after disengagement (page 75).

questionBank.q: When may customer information be disclosed to third parties?
opts: When required by law, professional responsibility, authorised by customer, or under enforceable subpoena.
When the customer has a low balance.
questionBank.exp: Disclosure is permitted when required by law, professional responsibility, authorised by customer, or in response to subpoena (page 75).

questionBank.q: Where should confidential customer information NOT be discussed?
opts: In elevators, lunchrooms, corridors, or social functions.
questionBank.exp: Non-public information must not be discussed in public places such as elevators, lunchrooms, corridors, or social functions (page 75).

questionBank.q: What is the rule regarding an officer's personal interest conflicting with duties?
opts: It must not conflict with any of their duties as an Officer of the Bank.
It is allowed if approved by a supervisor.
It is acceptable if it brings profit.
It is allowed if not disclosed.
questionBank.exp: The personal interest of an Officer shall not conflict with any of their duties (page 76).

questionBank.q: What is the Bank's policy on discrimination and harassment?
opts: It is not tolerated; the Bank values diversity and equal opportunity.
It is only prohibited in senior roles.
questionBank.exp: The Bank does not tolerate discrimination or harassment of any kind (page 76).

questionBank.q: What must an officer do before acquiring a financial interest in a business that does business with the Bank?
opts: Fully disclose the interest in writing to the Company Secretary.
Get approval from the branch manager.
questionBank.exp: Any financial interest in a business that does business with the Bank must be fully disclosed to the Company Secretary (page 76).

questionBank.q: What does 'Tipping off' refer to in a compliance context?
opts: Hinting to someone that they are under suspicion of money laundering or investigation.
questionBank.exp: Tipping off means doing or saying anything that might hint someone they are under suspicion of ML (page 77).

questionBank.q: Why is 'Tipping off' prohibited?
opts: Because it can warn suspects and undermine investigations.
Because it is not allowed by HR policy.
Because it is a security breach only.
questionBank.exp: Tipping off is prohibited because it warns suspects and undermines investigations (page 77).

questionBank.q: What is the rule regarding the use of staff accounts by third parties?
opts: Officers shall not allow their accounts to be used by third parties.
It is allowed for family members only.
It is allowed if below a certain amount.
It is allowed with branch manager approval.
questionBank.exp: Officers shall not allow any of their accounts to be used by third parties (page 77).

questionBank.q: What is the rule on 'Corporate Opportunity' for officers of the Bank?
opts: Prohibited from benefiting from opportunities arising from Bank property or position without CEO consent.
Allowed if the opportunity is profitable.
Allowed if not noticed by others.
questionBank.exp: Officers are prohibited from benefiting from opportunities using Bank property/position without CEO or Board Audit Committee consent (page 77).

questionBank.q: What is the transaction threshold for a General Manager (GM) for staff account lodgments?
questionBank.exp: The threshold for GM is N9,500,000 (page 78).

questionBank.q: What is the transaction threshold for a Deputy General Manager (DGM)?
questionBank.exp: The threshold for DGM is N5,000,000 (page 78).

questionBank.q: What is the transaction threshold for non-professional staff (ETD)?
questionBank.exp: The threshold for ETD (non-professional) is N2,000,000 (page 78).

questionBank.q: What action is taken for a first offence of exceeding staff account threshold without approval?
questionBank.exp: 1st Offender receives a Caution memo; 2nd: Warning memo; 3rd: Disciplinary Committee; 4th: Termination (page 79).

questionBank.q: What is the policy regarding dud cheque issuance by staff?
opts: No dud cheque issuance is permitted.
questionBank.exp: No dud cheque issuance is allowed for staff (page 79).

questionBank.q: What is the minimum period for retaining records of transactions after termination of a business relationship?
questionBank.exp: Records are kept for a minimum of five years after termination of business relationship (page 80).

questionBank.q: What is the requirement for recording and reporting of information by officers?
opts: Honest and accurate recording to make responsible business decisions.
Recording is optional for minor amounts.
questionBank.exp: Officers shall ensure honest and accurate recording of information (page 80).

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a serious offence according to the Bank's classification?
opts: Debiting a customer's account without consent.
questionBank.exp: Debiting customer's account without consent is a serious offence (page 89).

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a gross misconduct offence?
questionBank.exp: Tipping off to customers is listed as gross misconduct (page 90).

questionBank.q: What constitutes 'Gross Misconduct' in the disciplinary framework?
opts: Conduct so bad it destroys the employer/employee relationship and can lead to instant dismissal.
questionBank.exp: Gross misconduct destroys the employment relationship and can lead to instant dismissal (page 89).

questionBank.q: Which is an example of a minor offence?
questionBank.exp: Poor time keeping is a minor offence (page 89).

questionBank.q: What is the definition of bribery under the Bank's ethical standards?
opts: Providing a benefit to influence a public official to obtain an illegitimate business advantage.
Giving small gifts to family members.
questionBank.exp: Bribery is providing a benefit to influence a public official to circumvent the law (page 82).

questionBank.q: What was Access Bank's average CPI (Corruption Perception Index) score according to the 2023 report?
questionBank.exp: The Bank had an average CPI score of 40% in the 2023 report (page 83).

questionBank.q: Who is the appointed Anti-Bribery and Corruption Compliance Officer?
questionBank.exp: Inyang Etim (DGM) was appointed as the Anti-Bribery and Corruption Compliance Officer (page 86).

questionBank.q: What is the gift threshold for Senior Management (SM) and above?
questionBank.exp: The threshold for SM & above is N150,000 (page 87).

questionBank.q: What is the gift threshold for all other employees (Professional and support)?
questionBank.exp: The threshold for all other employees is N50,000 (page 87).

questionBank.q: Within how many working days must all employees declare a gift received?
questionBank.exp: All employees must declare gifts within 3 working days (page 87).

questionBank.q: What is the Gift Declaration Portal built on?
questionBank.exp: The Gift Declaration Portal is on ProcessMaker (page 87).

questionBank.q: When does accepting a gift become a bribery and corruption issue?
opts: When it is accepted without compliance with the Gift Policy.
Only when accepted from a government official.
questionBank.exp: It becomes bribery/corruption when gifts are accepted without following the policy (page 87).

questionBank.q: What is one benefit of having a Code of Ethics?
opts: Enhances reputation and builds trust internally and externally.
questionBank.exp: Benefits include enhanced reputation, trust, and reduced ethics risks (page 88).

questionBank.q: What is a key element of the Bank's Anti-Bribery & Corruption Program?
opts: Including specific ABC clauses in Service Level Agreements (SLA) with vendors.
questionBank.exp: Specific ABC clauses are included in SLA of vendors (page 86).

questionBank.q: Which of the following is an example of a gross misconduct offence?
opts: Wilful blindness relating to money laundering offences.
questionBank.exp: Wilful blindness relating to ML offences is gross misconduct (page 90).

questionBank.q: What is the sanction for a 4th offender who exceeds staff account lodgment limits without approval?
questionBank.exp: 4th Offender faces termination of appointment (page 79).

questionBank.q: What is the primary purpose of a whistleblowing programme in an organisation?
opts: To enable staff and stakeholders to report unethical conduct anonymously and confidentially.
To punish all staff for any violations.
To reduce the number of employees.
questionBank.exp: Whistleblowing enables reporting of unethical conduct and is key to good governance (page 92).

questionBank.q: Why do many people generally fail to report misconduct?
opts: They do not know the law.
They do not care about money.
questionBank.exp: Many do not report due to fear of victimisation (page 92).

questionBank.q: What is a key feature of an effective whistleblowing programme?
opts: Ability to report anonymously and confidentially.
Mandatory disclosure of the reporter's identity.
questionBank.exp: Anonymous and confidential reporting is a key feature (page 92).

questionBank.q: How is the whistleblower protected if they disclose their identity to KPMG Ethics?
opts: The identity will NOT be disclosed to Access Bank without written consent.
The identity is shared with the police.
questionBank.exp: Even if disclosed to KPMG, it will not be shared with Access Bank without written consent (page 93).

questionBank.q: Which statement supports the importance of reporting misconduct?
opts: Silence may imply that I condone or am a party to the misconduct.
Reporting always leads to job loss.
questionBank.exp: Silence may imply condoning the misconduct or being a party to it (page 94).

questionBank.q: What is one reason people choose not to report misconduct?
opts: Lack of trust in the system.
questionBank.exp: Lack of trust in the system is a common reason for not reporting (page 95).

questionBank.q: Which of the following can be reported through the whistleblowing channel?
opts: Fraud, bribery, corruption, conflicts of interest, and harassment.
questionBank.exp: The list includes fraud, bribery, corruption, conflicts, harassment, abuse of authority, etc. (page 97).

questionBank.q: What is the procedure after calling the Deloitte Reporting Line?
opts: The operator interviews you and gives a reference number (PIN) for follow-up.
Your identity is recorded and shared with the Bank.
You must send a written formal letter.
questionBank.exp: You are interviewed, given a PIN, and can call back for feedback (page 98).

questionBank.q: Why will Deloitte not call the whistleblower back?
opts: Because it does not know the identity of the caller.
questionBank.exp: Deloitte does not know the identity since calls are anonymous (page 98).

questionBank.q: What email address is used for whistleblowing reports at Access Bank?
questionBank.exp: Reports are sent to tip-offs@deloitte.com.ng (page 98).

questionBank.q: How can a whistleblower report misconduct via the website?
opts: Log on to www.accessbankplc.com, click Customer Service then Whistle Blower, fill the form and submit.
Send a direct message on social media.
questionBank.exp: Go to the website, navigate Customer Service → Whistle Blower, fill the form (page 98).

questionBank.q: What is a critical success factor for the whistleblowing mechanism?
opts: Trust the Deloitte Reporting Line and provide detailed information.
Only report if there is a reward.
questionBank.exp: Critical success factors include trusting the line and providing detailed information (page 100).

questionBank.q: What should a whistleblower do when making a report to Deloitte?
opts: Provide nature of incident, people involved, dates, place, and how it occurred.
Only state the name of the culprit.
questionBank.exp: Provide all details: nature, people, dates, place, how it occurred (page 98).

questionBank.q: What is the consequence of failure to report misconduct?
opts: It may cast doubt on your integrity and loyalty.
It is encouraged by the Bank.
questionBank.exp: Failure to report may cast doubt on integrity and loyalty to the Bank (page 94).

questionBank.q: Who is protected by the whistleblowing policy?
questionBank.exp: The policy enables staff and stakeholders to report (page 92).

questionBank.q: What can a whistleblower use to hide their identity when calling?
opts: Hide the caller ID or use a specially created email address.
Use their personal phone without hiding.
questionBank.exp: You can hide caller ID or use a specially created email address (page 93).

questionBank.q: Why should false and malicious allegations be avoided?
opts: Because they are unethical and waste resources, undermining the system.
Because they are difficult to prove.
Because they help to test the system.
questionBank.exp: Critical success factors include avoiding false and malicious allegations (page 100).

questionBank.q: What is the purpose of the reference PIN given after reporting?
opts: To allow the whistleblower to follow up on the report confidentially.
To identify the whistleblower to the Bank.
To confirm the call was received.
questionBank.exp: The PIN allows follow-up calls for feedback (page 98).

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a whistleblowing reportable incident?
opts: Leakage of confidential data and override of controls.
questionBank.exp: Leakage of confidential data and override of controls are reportable (page 97).

questionBank.q: What is 'Swallowing the whistle' in the context of whistleblowing?
opts: Failing to report misconduct, which can lead to fraud and misconduct galore.
Accepting a bribe to stay silent.
questionBank.exp: 'Swallowing the whistle' means not reporting, leading to fraud and misconduct (page 94).

questionBank.q: What is one of the key elements of good corporate governance supported by whistleblowing?
opts: Good risk management including fraud and corruption mitigation.
questionBank.exp: Whistleblowing is key to good risk management for fraud, bribery, and corruption (page 92).

questionBank.q: What is the overarching message regarding compliance in the training?
opts: The culture of compliance, championed by Senior Management, is the focus for all officers.
Compliance is only for the Compliance department.
Profit is more important than compliance.
Regulators do not affect daily work.
questionBank.exp: The culture of compliance, championed by Senior Management, should be the focus of all officers (page 101).
